sn47.20:2.1: Woodward and Ṭhānissaro attribute the words to the crowd. I’m not sure which is correct, but I follow BB. See BB for notes on this and paramapasavani
sn47.20:2.2: _Janapadakalyāṇī_ is typically rendered as “the most beautiful lady in the land”. But here we see her talents as a dazzling singer and dancer. While she was famed for her beauty ([ud3.2:9.1]()), the word _kalyāṇa_ normally means “(morally) good, fine, lovely” and does not refer solely to her appearance.
